social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife in their own home
social_history.tobacco: Former smoker, quit 20 years ago (20 pack-years)
social_history.driving: Recently stopped driving due to unsafe gait

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive gait deterioration and mild memory problems for one year; admitted for tap trial evaluation
patient.history_present_illness: A 68-year-old right-handed retired civil engineer with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and benign prostatic hyperplasia was admitted for evaluation and high-volume tap trial for suspected normal pressure hydrocephalus. The patient reports approximately one year of progressive gait deterioration which has significantly affected his quality of life. His wife describes his gait as having become 'shuffling and unstable' — he takes small steps, rarely lifts his feet off the ground, and has had three falls in the past six months, including one that resulted in a bruised right elbow. He requires furniture or wall support to turn around. He has stopped walking outside unassisted and has not driven in four months after his wife expressed concern about unsafe driving. Concurrently, over approximately the same period, he has developed increasing difficulty with urinary urgency and incontinence. He has had five episodes of urinary incontinence in the past three months despite taking tamsulosin for BPH. His urologist has attributed the urinary incontinence to worsening BPH and added oxybutynin (which was subsequently stopped due to cognitive side effects). On cognitive assessment, his wife reports he is somewhat more forgetful than one year ago — primarily forgetting appointments and recently repeating questions — but he remains able to manage finances and plan. His primary care physician obtained a brain MRI 6 weeks ago which was reported as showing 'ventriculomegaly with mild white matter changes' and referred him for neurological evaluation. He was seen in outpatient neurology clinic, found to have an Evans index of 0.31 on review of imaging, and was admitted for tap trial.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and fully oriented. Speech fluent and coherent. MoCA 23/30 (loses points on delayed recall x3/5, trail-making, and visuospatial/clock drawing). MMSE 26/30. No aphasia, apraxia, or agnosia.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive, 3mm bilaterally. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. Facial sensation intact bilaterally. Tongue midline. Hearing intact to finger rub bilaterally.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk. Mild bilateral lower extremity tone increase (difficult to distinguish from rigidity vs passive resistance). Upper extremity tone normal. Strength 5/5 throughout. No tremor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Vibration reduced at toes bilaterally (age-appropriate). Light touch intact.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ biceps, triceps, brachioradialis bilaterally. Patellar 2+ bilaterally. Achilles 1+ bilaterally. Plantar flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose intact. Heel-shin mildly impaired on left.
neurological_exam.gait: Short-stepped, shuffling, wide-based gait (magnetic gait). Step height markedly reduced — feet barely clear the floor. Difficulty initiating gait ('gait freezing' at start). Slow cadence. Takes several steps to turn. Tandem gait impossible. Timed Up and Go test: 22 seconds.
neurological_exam.additional: No cogwheel rigidity. No resting tremor. No postural instability on pull test (does not fall backward).

findings.location: bilateral lateral ventricles and third ventricle

signal_characteristics.description: Enlarged lateral and third ventricles disproportionate to degree of cortical atrophy
Moderate periventricular FLAIR/T2 hyperintensity, moderate subcortical white matter changes
Mild thinning of corpus callosum body
Prominent CSF flow void at aqueduct

mri.impression: Findings borderline for normal pressure hydrocephalus. Evans index 0.31 (criterion is >0.3). Mild-to-moderate ventriculomegaly with mild tight high-convexity sulci pattern. Moderate periventricular and subcortical white matter disease which may represent concurrent small vessel ischemic disease. Corpus callosum mild thinning. Aqueductal flow void suggesting hyperdynamic pulsatility. The concurrent white matter disease complicates the NPH diagnosis. High-volume tap trial is appropriate next step. Clinical correlation recommended.

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 16 cmH2O. WBC: 1 cell/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 48 mg/dL. Glucose: 68 mg/dL (ratio 0.61). gram_stain: No organisms. cytology: No malignant cells. beta-amyloid_42: 718 pg/mL (borderline low-normal; reference >650). total_tau: 214 pg/mL (within normal limits; reference <300). phospho_tau: 34 pg/mL (normal; reference <61). 14-3-3_protein: Negative.

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume lumbar puncture tap trial with gait analysis

findings.gait_description: Post-tap: improved step height, slightly longer stride, less freezing, able to turn in fewer steps

findings.cognitive_assessment: MoCA pre-tap 23/30; MoCA 24 hours post-tap 24/30 — marginal improvement (1 point)

specialized_test.impression: Tap trial shows modest but clinically meaningful gait improvement at 24 hours (25% improvement in TUG, 21% improvement in 10-meter walk). Cognitive improvement is marginal (1 MoCA point). A positive tap trial (gait improvement >20% in TUG) supports NPH diagnosis and predicts shunt response. The equivocal cognitive improvement and the concurrent white matter disease suggest that some of his symptoms may be related to vascular disease. Overall, tap trial result is 'equivocal-positive' supporting NPH as likely contributor. VP shunt should be discussed with patient and family.
recommended_actions: Discuss VP shunt with patient and family
Consider amyloid PET to evaluate for concurrent Alzheimer's pathology

output.tracer_or_protocol: CSF flow quantification at aqueduct of Sylvius

findings.finding: Hyperdynamic aqueductal CSF flow consistent with NPH physiology

output.impression: Phase-contrast MRI demonstrates hyperdynamic aqueductal CSF flow with peak velocity 22 cm/s (>18 cm/s criterion) and net stroke volume 72 mcL/cycle (>42 mcL/cycle criterion). These findings are supportive of NPH pathophysiology. Together with the equivocal-positive tap trial and borderline Evans index, this supports the diagnosis of probable iNPH and favors VP shunting.
recommended_actions: VP shunt placement with pressure-adjustable valve

findings.finding: Mild-moderate diffuse amyloid uptake in frontal and parietal cortices
findings.interpretation: Mild amyloid accumulation above threshold — positive amyloid PET

findings.finding: Relatively preserved — typical of Alzheimer's amyloid pattern

quantitative_data.CL_score: 42 (above threshold of 24.4 CL for amyloid positivity)

output.impression: Positive amyloid PET (CL 42 — above threshold). This finding indicates concurrent Alzheimer's amyloid pathology in addition to NPH. The combination of NPH and Alzheimer's amyloid copathology reduces the predicted response rate to VP shunting. Overall shunt response rate is approximately 40-60% lower when amyloid PET is positive. This should be disclosed to the patient and family as part of shared decision-making for shunt placement.
recommended_actions: Disclose amyloid PET results to patient and family
Discuss realistic expectations for shunt response given amyloid copathology
Neuropsychological testing to establish cognitive baseline pre-shunt

findings.pre_tap: Moderately impaired — encoding and retrieval both impaired
findings.post_tap: Mildly improved encoding, retrieval still impaired

output.impression: Neuropsychological profile shows frontal-subcortical cognitive dysfunction (executive function, processing speed) with some episodic memory impairment — pattern consistent with NPH. Modest cognitive improvement post-tap (ADAS-cog 3 points). Memory impairment exceeds what is expected for pure NPH and may reflect concurrent Alzheimer's pathology (consistent with positive amyloid PET). Cognitive prognosis with shunting is guarded given amyloid copathology.
recommended_actions: Consider memantine for Alzheimer's component if symptoms progress
Genetic counseling regarding APOE status if desired

output.test_type: Extended external lumbar drainage trial (72 hours)

findings.day_1: 150 mL drained; TUG improved from 22 to 16 sec (27%)

findings.day_2: 160 mL drained; TUG 15.2 sec (31% improvement from baseline)

findings.day_3: 155 mL drained; TUG 14.8 sec (33% improvement from baseline)

findings.cognitive_change: MoCA improved from 23 to 25/30 over 72h drainage period

output.impression: Extended 72-hour external lumbar drainage trial confirms NPH diagnosis with progressive and sustained gait improvement (33% TUG improvement). Cognitive improvement of 2 MoCA points also noted. This sustained response to prolonged CSF drainage strengthens the case for VP shunt placement and improves predicted shunt response rate.
recommended_actions: VP shunt placement recommended based on positive extended drainage trial

findings.finding: Detrusor overactivity (neurogenic overactive bladder) — involuntary detrusor contractions at 200 mL fill
Reduced first sensation of filling at 100 mL (normal 150-200 mL)
No bladder outlet obstruction pattern despite BPH

output.impression: Urodynamics demonstrates neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO) with involuntary detrusor contractions — consistent with NPH-associated urinary incontinence from frontal inhibitory pathway dysfunction. No bladder outlet obstruction despite known BPH. The NDO pattern supports NPH over isolated BPH as the primary cause of urinary incontinence.
recommended_actions: Discontinue tamsulosin if shunting proceeds and NDO improves
Bladder diary and post-void residual monitoring

output.proposed: Perioperative antibiotics for VP shunt placement (cefazolin 2g IV)
interactions: Metformin: hold for 48h perioperatively if contrast used; cefazolin has no interaction
warnings: Lisinopril may cause perioperative hypotension — discuss with anesthesia

differential.diagnosis: Vascular dementia / subcortical ischemic vascular disease
differential.key_features: Moderate white matter disease, hypertension, diabetes — but Evans index >0.3, classic triad, positive tap trial support NPH; vascular disease may be co-contributor
Episodic memory impairment, family history of AD, positive amyloid PET — but gait apraxia and magnetic gait are more prominent early than in typical AD; NPH-AD copathology likely
Shuffling gait — but no resting tremor, no cogwheel rigidity, no bradykinesia, no asymmetry; ventriculomegaly supports NPH
Gait disorder — but no upper motor neuron signs, no Lhermitte sign, no hyperreflexia; MRI shows ventriculomegaly not cord compression

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Evans index 0.31, ventriculomegaly, mild white matter disease, aqueductal flow void

optimal_actions.action: Comprehensive labs to exclude reversible causes
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal B12, TSH, RPR; diabetic HbA1c

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal opening pressure, normal CSF; equivocal-positive gait improvement (25%)

tool_parameters.gait_assessment: TUG and 10m walk before and after

optimal_actions.action: Neuropsychological testing pre and post tap
Phase-contrast MRI for CSF flow quantification
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Hyperdynamic aqueductal flow — supportive of NPH

optimal_actions.action: Amyloid PET to evaluate for concurrent Alzheimer's pathology
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Positive amyloid PET — reduces predicted shunt response

optimal_actions.action: Urodynamic study to characterize neurogenic bladder
VP shunt referral after positive tap trial and drainage trial

critical_actions: High-volume tap trial with formal gait assessment is mandatory for NPH evaluation
Measure Evans index and callosal angle on MRI
Exclude reversible causes (hypothyroid, B12 deficiency, neurosyphilis)
Concurrent white matter disease and amyloid PET positivity should be disclosed to patient — may reduce shunt benefit
Urodynamics to confirm neurogenic detrusor overactivity vs BPH as incontinence cause
contraindicated_actions: Diagnosing and treating as Parkinson's disease with levodopa without evidence of DaTscan abnormality or tremor
VP shunt without formal tap trial or high clinical suspicion for NPH
Attributing all urinary symptoms to BPH without urodynamic evaluation in suspected NPH
key_reasoning_points: Moderate case — Evans index is borderline (0.31), white matter disease is present as potential confounding diagnosis, tap trial shows modest but positive response (25%)
Amyloid PET positivity indicates concurrent Alzheimer's pathology — this is the moderate-difficulty element as it complicates prognosis
Phase-contrast MRI with hyperdynamic aqueductal flow (peak velocity 22 cm/s) provides additional supportive evidence for NPH physiology
The concurrent white matter disease (from hypertension and diabetes) may contribute independently to gait and cognitive impairment
Neurogenic detrusor overactivity on urodynamics confirms the bladder dysfunction is from NPH-related frontal pathway disease, not isolated BPH

red_herrings.data_point: Benign prostatic hyperplasia with tamsulosin prescription
red_herrings.intended_effect: Urinary incontinence attributed to worsening BPH rather than NPH
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Urodynamics shows neurogenic detrusor overactivity pattern, not outlet obstruction — urinary incontinence is from NPH-related frontal dysfunction, not BPH

red_herrings.intended_effect: Family history prompts Alzheimer's diagnosis over NPH
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: While positive amyloid PET suggests some Alzheimer's copathology, the dominant syndrome (gait apraxia, incontinence, ventriculomegaly, positive tap trial) is NPH; NPH-AD copathology is recognized

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Moderate NPH — Evans index borderline (0.31), moderate white matter disease, equivocal-positive tap trial (25%), positive amyloid PET suggesting NPH-AD copathology.
